text:
[LERR.1.4.7] **Shape.** A `ComputationError` event lands in the
event trace (per [LFST])
with kind, rule / activation / slot context, and
source-location reference through the ruleset
hash. A `ComputationError` abandons the failing
activation and the rule cycle continues past it —
rung 6, and the cost stops at the activation
([LERR.1]). Where engine state is no longer
trustworthy (an artefact whose values contradict its
own types, memory exhaustion with no declared cap, an
engine invariant found broken ([IERR.1.7]), a
`pump_wcet_ns` overrun — [RTCT.7.3])
the disposition is an `EngineError` and the engine
halts the tier — rung 7.

**The halt stops the work in progress where it is raised.** Unlike rungs 5 and 6, the rule cycle does not continue past it. From
the `EngineError` on, the engine **must** run no further action of the
activation that raised it, fire no further activation, propagate no further
fact, and record nothing more, not even that activation's close. That binds
inside a fact change already under way: the engine **must not** carry the
change that raised it any further, through the network, into the retractions it
would cascade into, or on to the rest of a sweep, an upsert or a clock step. So
the `EngineError` is the last record of the tier.

**After the halt, the engine's state is undefined, except that it is halted.**
The engine **may** leave working memory, its
agenda and every series in whatever state the halt found them, and two engines
halted by one input **may** hold different states. What a host may still call
is [NCBK.2.9]'s.
